To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
market power in the generation of data is a significant factor in the competition for data privacy.

(1) the relationship between market structure and data privacy is not well understood, (2) market power in data generation services is not necessarily associated with market power in data privacy, (3) market power in underlying services may be used to restrict competition in data privacy, and (4) competition law can be used to promote competition in data privacy.

the lack of competition and/or the existence of market power in the services that generate data can lead to a reduction in the level of data protection, as firms will be less incentivized to invest in privacy protection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1. The relationship between market structure and the level of data protection and deployment of PETs 2. The role of competition law in promoting competition through data privacy
the question whether competition on data privacy and PET deployment can be enhanced through a more effective application of competition law.

the role of competition policy in ensuring effective competition through data protection and PETs, and in particular with the extent to which the existing tools and concepts of competition law are adequate for that purpose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
competition in data privacy is not a zero price market.
market power in data privacy and the use of PETs is a function of a variety of structural and behavioural factors.

market power in data markets can affect competition in data privacy, and that competition law is an appropriate instrument for promoting and maintaining such a competition, but that further research is necessary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the market for data privacy is characterized by the presence of network effects, and that the presence of such effects is likely to increase the market power of dominant players.
market power in the data generation services can be a significant barrier to competition in data privacy, and that competition law can help to promote and maintain such competition.
the market structure of the underlying markets that generate data is an important determinant of competition in data privacy, but that it is not the only one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
market structure is an imperfect proxy for market power, especially when it comes to assessing competition on data privacy.
the current proxies for market power in the services that generate data may not be adequate to capture the market power in data privacy and PETS.
the current competition law framework, which focuses on market power and price competition, is ill equipped to address the concerns raised in the article.
